messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SEV-2 - host-gpu-17 reported KERNEL_PANIC and Kubelet NotReady in us-west-2, affected node in gpu-pool-3. Alert ID: PD-9928
PagerDuty: New incident: PD-9928 - host-gpu-17 kernel panic (auto-page to eng-oncall)
Alex K: acked. I'm oncall for night, looking now.
oncall-backup: noted, jumping in if needed.
Alex K: quick status -- node is flapping, metric shows node_exporter disappeared at 03:12 UTC then kernel oops at 03:13. Kubelet transitions NotReady about 03:14.
Mira P: @Alex K any customer-facing errors / 5xx spikes?
Alex K: checking LB logs and API gateway. So far ~8% of requests in the gpu-pool-3 route have 503s over last 5m. Likely due to capacity drop; not full cluster outage.
Jordan L: paging infra team; if host is kernel panic might need rebuild. pinging infra-bot for inventory.
infra-bot: host-gpu-17 -> AWS instance i-0b3f91a2. Attached hardware: p4d. Host responded to hypervisor but no SSH since 03:13. Console logs show: 
```
[    123.456789] NVRM: Xid (0001:0a) GPU fault: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU lockup
[    123.457801] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
Call Trace:
  dump_stack+0x64/0x90
  panic+0x1c5/0x3d0
```
Alex K: thanks. I'll try to gracefully cordon the node and shift workloads. If kubelet is down drain might hang.
Alex K: `kubectl cordon host-gpu-17` -> node marked Unschedulable (ok).
Alex K: `kubectl drain host-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> drain stuck waiting for pods with local storage (some model caches).
Sam R: can we evict with `--grace-period=30 --force`? risk of losing cached KV but speeds recovery.
Mira P: agree for production traffic. Customer impact minimal if we failover models to smaller variant; do it.
Alex K: running `kubectl drain host-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30` now.
Alex K: drain completed, scheduler rescheduled pods to gpu-pool-2 and gpu-pool-4. Token latency for affected routes rose ~120ms while warmup happened.
Jordan L: infra requested serial console screenshot and kernel dump. infra-bot: creating case with host support, snapshotting instance store.
infra-bot: support case created CS-5542. Serial log archived: https://internal-logs/reports/CS-5542/host-gpu-17/console.txt
Mira P: quick customer summary for ops: impacted a subset of Dedicated customers in us-west-2 using p4-backed Dedicated pools, ~8% error rate for 10m window, auto-failed over to other pools, mitigation applied, no data loss reported.
Alex K: updating incident channel for PG. Adding temporary routing rule to avoid scheduling to gpu-pool-3 until further notice.
oncall-backup: noted, promoting to follow-up for morning handoff.
PagerDuty: PD-9928 status changed to acknowledged by Alex K (03:18 UTC)
Sam R: any sign this is a widespread kernel regression? we saw similar stack in last month but on different driver pack.
Jordan L: I'll check recent host kernel/driver rollouts: nothing scheduled for us-west-2 this week. Could be hw degradation on that specific host.
Alex K: verifying model restarts and llm cache warms. dd-agent logs show some eviction but overall successful restarts.
Alex K: running healthcheck script against affected models: `./healthcheck.sh --region us-west-2 --pool gpu-pool-3` -> returns some pods NotReady but others OK.
Mira P: I'm going to prepare an incident note for customers (short) and post in #customer-success. Draft: "We experienced a kernel panic on a single GPU host in us-west-2 which briefly reduced capacity for some Dedicated pools. Traffic was rerouted, and normal service resumed with minor latency increase. No data loss. We're investigating root cause and will follow up"
Sam R: good. Add ETA for follow-up: kernel oops analysis and host repair timeline (T-12h) or earlier.
Jordan L: infra-bot: reimage scheduled? Recommended host reimage to ensure clean state.
infra-bot: recommended action: reprovision instance i-0b3f91a2 with fresh AMI and drivers; schedule window 04:30 UTC.
Alex K: OK. I'll remove host-gpu-17 from cluster (terminate) after snapshot and then let infra reprovision. For now we've pinned scheduler to avoid pool.
Mira P: handing off to daytime oncall @oncall-backup for follow-up. Summary for handoff: PD-9928, kernel panic host-gpu-17 (i-0b3f91a2). Impact: ~8% 503s for 10m window for Dedicated us-west-2 pool; mitigated by draining and rescheduling; reimage planned 04:30 UTC; support case CS-5542 opened; no customer data loss.
oncall-backup: I have it. Will monitor reprovision, confirm when reimage completes, and update customer note with timeline.
PagerDuty: PD-9928 status changed to resolved by Alex K (03:41 UTC) -- note: resolved here means active mitigation complete; follow-up tasks remain.
Alex K: closing the on-call loop. Thanks all. Leaving follow-up list:
- infra: reimage and driver validation on i-0b3f91a2 (CS-5542)
- eng-runtime: check recent kernel/driver compatibility with p4d AMI, cross-check with last month kernel-oops signatures
- devex: confirm routing rule rollback once pool healthy
- postmortem owner: Jordan L (draft due in 48h)
Jordan L: will take postmortem. Question for runtime team: capture full dmesg and crash dump before reimage if possible.
infra-bot: snapshot created and available at s3://host-dumps/CS-5542/host-gpu-17-snapshot.tar.gz
Sam R: flagging as recurring-risk if we see more kernel oops with same Xid. We'll track in reliability board.
Mira P: thanks everyone. I'll push short customer note in ~30m after we confirm reimage schedule.
oncall-backup: accepted handoff at 03:47 UTC. Monitoring alarms suppressed on this host and pool for maintenance window.
Alex K: ending thread. :white_check_mark:
